topic.label: Startups
topic.desc: Startups: idea validation, product and MVP, growth analytics, finance and runway, fundraising, and company operations.

concepts: Testing whether a problem is real and a market is large enough before building.
Scoping a minimum viable product, prioritizing a roadmap and running the issue tracker.
Funnels, retention and experiments from product analytics.
Burn, runway, unit economics and revenue monitoring.
Investor research, pitch narrative and data-room preparation.
Hiring plans, objectives and investor updates that keep a small team aligned.
skills: Turns customer-interview notes into recurring problems, current workarounds and quotes, and marks which findings rest on one interview only.
Estimates market size top-down and bottom-up with every assumption listed and a range instead of one number.
Maps direct and indirect competitors, their funding and positioning from company data, and the gap the startup targets.
Cuts a product idea down to the smallest release that tests the riskiest assumption, with what is deliberately left out.
Ranks backlog items by impact, effort and risk and shows the scoring so the founders can overrule it.
Creates, labels and triages issues and sprint cycles in the team's tracker and reports what is blocked.
Builds the signup-to-activation funnel from product events and finds the biggest drop-off with its sample size.
Computes retention by signup cohort and reports whether the curve flattens, with the cohort sizes behind each line.
Designs a growth experiment with a hypothesis, metric and stopping rule and reads the result without peeking early.
Models monthly burn and runway under base, slow and fast cases and shows the month cash reaches zero in each.
Computes acquisition cost, margin and payback per customer segment from billing and spend data and flags thin samples.
Reads billing data for balance, new subscriptions, refunds and failed payments and reports changes against last month.
Builds an investor list by stage, sector and recent deals from company data, with the source of each fit claim.
Structures the pitch narrative and slide list, tying every claim to a metric or source.
Lists the documents an investor will request, tracks which exist and who owns the missing ones.
Sequences the first hires by what they unblock and what each costs against runway.
Drafts quarterly objectives and measurable key results and checks that each key result has an owner and a data source.
Writes a monthly investor update from metrics and decisions, stating what went wrong as plainly as what went right.
